name: Unit RFID2
summary: Reads tag IDs and can read or write user data on compatible 13.56 MHz tags at close range.

kit_stickers.contents: The CoreS3/StickS3 hackathon kit guide lists four adhesive tags. Their individual chip types and lock states need identification.
kit_stickers.use_by_id: An app can assign an action to the tag's existing ID without writing to it.
kit_stickers.use_by_data: A compatible writable tag can carry short text or a URL as an NFC record (NDEF). The first example reads IDs. A write and read-back still needs physical validation.

interface.range_note: Manufacturer specifies less than 20 mm; not a phone/NFC compatibility guarantee.

host_bindings.notes: External bus; do not reinitialize internal I2C on GPIO12/11.
USB-powered bring-up: enable EXT_5V output after M5.begin when powering the unit from StickS3. Do not feed external power into an output-enabled Grove port.

support.meaning: Primary-source review plus separately labeled vendor bench notes. No accessory driver or emulator input is implemented; vendor results are not plugin physical acceptance.

first_hardware_check: Check external bus acknowledgement at 0x28. Use an I2C RFID driver, not an SPI-only RC522 example.
Read UID from a supplied compatible tag; remove and re-present it; display a no-card state. Start read-only.
troubleshooting: UID presence is not secure authentication. Do not default to card writing or key/sector changes.
Vendor page lists Type A/B, while its FAQ and RC522-style examples focus on Type A/MIFARE/NTAG. Treat other tag protocols as unverified until tested.
RFID U031, RFID2 U031-B and UHF RFID are different parts.
Start with a known Type A test tag. 125 kHz and UHF tags use incompatible radio bands; do not diagnose them as wiring faults. Test absent-reader recovery without writing card memory.

app_fixture_plan.note: Label simulated identifiers; preserve UID length and leading zero bytes. No RF or card-memory emulation.

sources.title: NTAG213, NTAG215 and NTAG216 user memory and NFC data format
sources.author: NXP Semiconductors

libraries.author: kkloesener and upstream MFRC522 authors
libraries.purpose: Vendor-reported candidate, not compiled into this plugin. Inspect current bus injection, reset timeout and source notices; pin a reviewed commit in the app before reuse.

vendor_bench_report.scope: Reported observations from a separate vendor build; not plugin driver or physical acceptance.
notes: RFID2 was tested on StickS3 Grove SDA9/SCL10; the vendor read NTAG215 using an MFRC522 I2C implementation.
The selected driver polls ISO14443 Type A; this does not validate Type B even though the WS1850S hardware manual lists A/B.
The supplied kit guide reports four adhesive tags. Check the actual box; this is not a guaranteed RFID2 retail package quantity.
The vendor warns that PCD_Reset in its selected driver can wait indefinitely if the reader is absent. Review and bound initialization before relying on it.
